title: Al-Mutaffifin: the rust on hearts
hookLine: what they earned has rusted over their hearts (83:14)

cards: Leave a bike out in the rain for one night and nothing happens. Leave it out all winter and you come back to a chain that won't turn. Rust doesn't arrive in a day.
It comes a speck at a time, each speck too small to bother with, until the thing doesn't move anymore.
Al-Mutaffifin uses that same picture, one anyone who's owned something metal will know, for what a tiny cheat, repeated, does: not to the customer, but to the one doing it.

teach.b: The surah describes people who hear its verses recited and say: stories of the ancients. Old tales, nothing to do with me.
Verse fourteen explains why, in Pickthall's words: Nay, but that which they have earned is rust upon their hearts.

The Arabic word is rana, a covering, a film, a crust that forms over something and dulls it. It isn't that they can't hear. What they've done has built up, layer on layer, until the heart doesn't catch the light anymore.
A hadith in Tirmidhi turns the verse into a picture.

teach.h: A BLACK SPOT, OR POLISHED CLEAN.
teach.b: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said that when a person does wrong, a black spot is put on the heart. If he stops, asks forgiveness and turns back, the heart is polished clean.
If he goes back to it, the spot grows, until it covers the heart. And that, he said, is the rana that God mentions.
So the picture has two halves: hearts rust, and hearts shine. Turning back, tawbah, is the polish. So is remembrance of God, which some scholars describe as the heart's cleaning cloth.
The man skimming a pinch off every sale doesn't feel like a villain. Each pinch is a speck. But the specks add up, not only in the ledger but in him, until the verses sound like old stories.
And a few verses later the surah describes the other record, of the righteous, and says: for this, let those who compete, compete.

how: Muslims speak of polishing the heart through tawbah, turning back, and dhikr, remembrance; saying astaghfirullah, I seek God's forgiveness, through the day is one way this is done, recalling the hadith of the black spot that is wiped clean.

o: the skimmers, those who give short measure
the hypocrites, who pray only to be seen
the generous, who give more than they owe

games.q: what's inside the verse — tap the pairs.
p: a crust that dulls the heart

s: the rust on the heart is permanent
the hadith says turning back and asking forgiveness polishes it clean.
a hadith links the black spot on the heart to the rana of 83:14
the Prophet said the growing spot is the rana God mentions (Tirmidhi).
the people in the surah can't hear the verses
they hear them, and call them old stories. the rust dulls, it doesn't deafen.

games.q: a black spot has been put on a heart by a wrong. according to the hadith, what cleans it?
o: stopping, asking forgiveness and turning back
doing twice as many good deeds first
games.why: if he stops, asks forgiveness and turns back, the heart is polished (Tirmidhi). if he returns to it, the spot grows.

practice: Think of one small habit that's been building up quietly, a little dishonesty, a daily irritation you feed, a thing you keep meaning to stop, and picture it as one spot on something that should shine.
Then picture a cloth, and one slow wipe. If you pray, you can say astaghfirullah, I seek God's forgiveness.

wordCard.voice: Al-Mutaffifin. Those who skim, Surah eighty-three, which says what they earned became rust on their hearts. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: "covered over, rusted," a crust that dulls a surface (Qur'an 83:14).

carryVoice: Your line: hearts rust; hearts shine. In the hadith, the rust can still come off. Day two hundred nine.

sources.q: Nay, but that which they have earned is rust upon their hearts.
